metadata.name: Myasthenia Gravis Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL) Profile
metadata.summary: 8-item patient-reported outcome (0–24) assessing ocular, bulbar, respiratory, and limb symptoms over the past 7 days.
clinical_pearls: A change of >= 2 points is considered clinically meaningful.
Any breathing (score >= 2) or swallowing impairment warrants urgent evaluation for impending myasthenic crisis.
Distilled from 8 patient-reported items of the 13-item Quantitative Myasthenia Gravis (QMG) scale.
Pitfall — Ceiling & ocular effects: Discrimination is limited above ~20 points (ceiling effect), and purely ocular MG (ptosis/diplopia) may be underrated; axial weakness is not assessed.

Pitfall — Linear weighting & comorbidities: Equal 0–3 scoring per item can understate critical deficits (e.g., ventilator dependence), while non-MG comorbidities (arthritis, stroke, depression) can falsely elevate the total; do not use alone to triage impending crisis.

options.label: Constant slurring or nasal speech, but can be understood
Frequent choking necessitating changes in diet

items.label: Impairment of Ability to Brush Teeth or Comb Hair

options.label: Extra effort, but no rest periods needed
Cannot do one of these functions

items.label: Impairment of Ability to Arise from a Chair

interpretation.label: Mild Symptom Burden (2–4)
interpretation.summary: Mild functional limitation in daily activities.

interpretation.label: Moderate Symptom Burden (5–9)
interpretation.summary: Moderate symptom burden; review immunotherapy optimization.

interpretation.label: Severe Symptom Burden (>= 10)
interpretation.summary: High symptom burden; screen closely for bulbar/respiratory crisis.

assessment_guides.title: MG-ADL 7-Day Recall & Crisis Screening
bedside_steps: Ask the patient to rate their typical status over the preceding 7 days (not just a single transient moment).
pitfalls_and_exceptions: Score 2 or 3 on Breathing or Swallowing requires immediate FVC/NIF assessment regardless of total score.
Ensure ocular diplopia resolves with monocular occlusion.
